questions.question:
An employee complained to his company's human resources department that the company employed undocumented immigrants. Unbeknownst to the employee, the company was currently engaged in a class action lawsuit in which it stood accused of conspiring to lower its employees' wages by hiring undocumented workers. The company's attorney met with the employee and pressured him to recant his complaint, so it would not be used against the company in the class action lawsuit. The employee refused, and he was subsequently fired.
The employee sued the company in federal court, alleging that his termination violated federal law. During discovery, the employee requested that the company turn over all documents and information concerning the company's decision to fire him. The company refused on the ground that the information was protected by the attorney-client privilege. The employee then filed a motion to compel production. The district court entered an order granting the employee's motion on the ground that the company waived this privilege. The company immediately filed a notice of appeal on the ground that the order constituted a collateral order.
Will the appellate court likely hear the appeal?

choices.A: No, because the collateral-order doctrine is not expressly authorized by a federal statute.
choices.B: No, because this issue can be effectively reviewed on appeal from the final judgment.
choices.C: Yes, because an appellate court decision on this issue will likely resolve the dispute.
choices.D: Yes, because due process requires that the appellate court immediately hear the appeal.

Final-judgment rule
Did court enter final judgment?
  • Decision fully resolves the merits of a dispute, leaving nothing but enforcement
Yes → Appeal allowed
No
Does exception apply?
  • Injunction (grant/denial)
  • Certification by district court
  • Class action certification
  • Appointment of receiver
  • Admiralty cases
  • Collateral-order doctrine
  • Bankruptcy cases (certain orders)
  • Mandamus (petition for writ)
  • Patent-infringement order (accounting left)
  • Mnemonic: In Certain Circumstances,
    An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely
Yes → Appeal allowed
No
No appeal

Absent narrow exceptions, 28 U.S.C. § 1291 limits appeals to final judgments—ie, decisions that fully resolve a dispute on the merits and leave nothing for the district court to do but enforce the judgment. One such exception is the collateral-order doctrine, which allows an interlocutory appeal when:

• a district court order conclusively resolves an important issue
• that issue is separate from the merits of the underlying claim and
• that order is effectively unreviewable on appeal from a final judgment.

In Mohawk Indus., Inc. v. Carpenter, the Supreme Court held that a district court's order rejecting a party's attorney-client privilege claim (as seen here) is not a collateral order. That is because this important issue, though separate from the merits, can be effectively reviewed on appeal from the final judgment. For example, if the appellate court finds the privilege applicable, it can remand the case for a new trial without the privileged evidence. Therefore, the appellate court likely will not hear the company's appeal under the collateral-order doctrine.

(Choice A) Most exceptions to the final-judgment rule are expressly authorized in 28 U.S.C. § 1292 (eg, district court certification) or other federal statutes (eg, certain orders in bankruptcy cases). Although the collateral-order doctrine is not expressly authorized by a federal statute, it is still a valid exception to the final-judgment rule because it was established by the Supreme Court.

(Choice C) Even if an appellate court decision on the privilege issue would resolve the parties' dispute, it would not provide a basis for an immediate appeal under the collateral-order doctrine.

(Choice D) Due process does not require the appellate court to immediately hear the appeal. Instead, appellate review will be available once the district court enters a final judgment.

📌 Educational Objective

The collateral-order doctrine is an exception to the final-judgment rule. It allows an appeal before final judgment when (1) a district court order conclusively resolves an important issue, (2) that issue is separate from the merits of the underlying claim, and (3) that order is effectively unreviewable on appeal from a final judgment.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1291 (final-judgment rule).
  • Cohen v. Beneficial Indus. Loan Corp., 337 U.S. 541, 545–46 (1949) (establishing the collateral-order doctrine).
  • Mohawk Indus., Inc. v. Carpenter, 558 U.S. 100, 109 (2009) (holding that a district court order denying a party's attorney-client privilege claim is not a collateral order subject to immediate appeal).

MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Appeals

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）相关的取证裁定，能不能按附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）立刻上诉。

三秒认题路径：

没终局 → 找例外 → 看三要件 → 卡在可复审 → 不能马上上诉

核心法律规则

一般规则是，28 U.S.C. § 1291 只允许对终局判决（final judgment）上诉，也就是案件在实体上已经结束、只剩执行。若不是终局判决，就只能看有没有法定中间上诉例外，或是否符合附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）。

这个原则要求：命令要重要、与实体争议分开，而且必须是effectively unreviewable；考试里这句话的意思不是“现在不爽”，而是“等案子结束后仍然救不回来”。

对律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）的披露命令，最高法院在 Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 里说：通常不能立刻上诉，因为终局后仍可通过撤销、发回重审或排除材料来补救。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter —— 认定拒绝特权主张的披露令通常不是可立即上诉的附带命令。

思维导图

先问：现在是终局判决吗？
Yes→ 终局已出，通常可上诉
No→ 继续找例外
有没有法定中间上诉？
比如 禁令（injunction）、认证（certification）、集体诉讼认证（class action certification） 等
本题没有 § 1292 的认证，也不是那类法定例外
再看 附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）
① 重要问题？② 与实体分离？③ effectively unreviewable？
本题死在第 ③ 步：终局后仍能救济，不算“不可复审”
结论：不能立即上诉 → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：披露了特权材料，秘密一旦出去就回不来了，所以应该马上上诉。

但考试真正问的是：终局后法院还能不能补救这次错误。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干是发现公司拒绝交付特权材料后，法院下令披露；这类命令终局后仍可救济，所以不满足立即上诉的条件。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“不是法条授权”当成“不能上诉”的唯一理由了。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ C: 误把“能解决争议”当成“能立刻上诉”。

❌ 事实误判 | 程序救济偷换

✕ D: 把due process当成即时上诉通道了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是终局；不是终局就只查法定例外和 collateral-order 第三要件。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”——只记住这些常考例外：禁令（injunction）、认证（certification）、集体诉讼认证（class action certification）等；但像本题这种特权披露令，通常还是等终局后再上诉。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A famous clothing designer was notified that a company had been manufacturing jeans with his trademarked symbol stitched into the waistband. The designer immediately filed an action in federal district court for trademark infringement, claiming monetary damages and an injunction. Following a hearing, the district court granted the designer a preliminary injunction and ordered the company to cease manufacturing the jeans at issue until a judgment was reached in the action. The company timely filed an immediate appeal of the district court's order issuing the preliminary injunction.
Can the court of appeals review the district court's order?

choices.A: No, because a final judgment was not rendered.
choices.B: No, because equitable orders are not immediately appealable.
choices.C: Yes, because an interlocutory order granting an injunction is immediately appealable.
choices.D: Yes, because it may hear any interlocutory appeal from the district court filed within 10 days of the date on which the appealed order was issued.

questions.explanation:
Final-judgment rule
Rule Appeal only allowed after final judgment
  • If multiple claims/parties, final judgment as to fewer than all claims/parties appropriate if court expressly determines no justifiable reason for delay
Exceptions Interlocutory appeals* concerning:
  • Injunction (grant/denial)
  • Certification by district court
  • Class action certification
  • Appointment of receiver
  • Admiralty case
  • Collateral-order doctrine
  • Bankruptcy cases (certain orders)
  • Mandamus (petition for writ)
  • Patent infringement order (only accounting left)
Mnemonic:  In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely
*Appeal from trial court ruling that occurs before entry of final judgment.

The final-judgment rule typically bars federal appellate courts from hearing an appeal until the district court has entered a final judgment—i.e., a judicial decision that fully resolves the dispute on the merits and leaves nothing for the court to do but enforce the judgment. However, there are exceptions to this rule that allow for an immediate, interlocutory appeal (see table above). One such exception permits an interlocutory appeal of a district court order that grants or denies a preliminary injunction.

Here, the district court granted the clothing designer a preliminary injunction that prohibited the company from manufacturing jeans during the pendency of the case. Although a final judgment has not yet been rendered, the order granting the injunction was immediately appealable (Choice A). As a result, the court of appeals can review the district court's order.

(Choice B) An equitable order awards nonmonetary relief when monetary damages are insufficient to redress the injury. And an order granting a preliminary injunction is an equitable order that can be immediately appealed.

(Choice D) An appellate court must hear certain interlocutory appeals filed within 30 days after the applicable order was issued. This includes an interlocutory appeal from an order granting or denying a preliminary injunction (as seen here). And an appellate court may hear an interlocutory appeal filed within 10 days of an order that a district court certified for appeal.

📌 Educational Objective

The final-judgment rule prohibits federal appellate courts from hearing an appeal until the district court has entered a final judgment unless an exception permits an immediate, interlocutory appeal. One such exception permits an interlocutory appeal of a district court order that grants or denies a preliminary injunction.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1292 (exceptions to final-judgment rule).

MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Interlocutory review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：临时禁令（preliminary injunction）是否属于可立刻上诉的中间裁定（interlocutory order）。

三秒认题路径：

未终局 → 看例外 → 禁令裁定 → 立即可上诉 → 选 C

核心法律规则

终局判决规则（final-judgment rule）的意思是：一般要等案件真正结束后才能上诉，考场意思：现在不能因为一个中间命令就随便上。

但禁令（injunction）的授予或拒绝是法定例外，考场意思：只要法官发的是禁令裁定，就能立刻进上诉程序。

所以本题里，地区法院已经下了初步禁令（preliminary injunction），公司可以马上上诉，不必等最终判决。

核心判例： 本题对应 28 U.S.C. § 1292(a)(1) 的法定例外；只要是“grant or deny an injunction”，就可立即上诉。

思维导图

先问：这是 最终判决（final judgment） 吗？
否一般不能上诉，先别被“案件还没结束”骗走。
再查有没有法定中间上诉例外 § 1292？
有：临时禁令（preliminary injunction）的授予/拒绝
卡死点：这里不需要等终局，直接能上诉
结论：上诉法院可以审查该命令 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：案件还没结案，final judgment 不存在，所以应该不能上诉。

但考试真正问的是：这个命令有没有落在“禁令例外”里；有的话，中间上诉（interlocutory appeal）就能走。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的商业损失已经发生了多少」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的preliminary injunction正是法定可立即上诉的禁令裁定，所以公司不用等最终判决。

❌ 概念混淆 | 终局误判

✕ A: 只盯着 final judgment，忘了禁令有例外。

❌ 法律适用 | 衡平泛化

✕ B: 把 equitable orders 一刀切成不能上诉。

❌ 事实误判 | 期限偷换

✕ D: 把 10 days 硬套到禁令上，期限和规则都错位了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否终局，再秒查法定禁令例外；只要是 injunction，先别被 final judgment 卡住。

考场速记

记住口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”，先想到 injunction、certification、class action 等法定中间上诉例外，再决定能不能立刻上诉。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
Two days before his home was to be sold at a foreclosure sale, a homeowner obtained a temporary restraining order (TRO) in federal court that prevented his lender from proceeding with the sale for 14 days or until a preliminary injunction hearing could take place, whichever was sooner. When a preliminary injunction hearing could not be scheduled within the original 14-day period, the court extended the TRO for another 30 days.
The lender appealed the court's order extending the TRO. The homeowner has moved to dismiss the appeal.
Is the appellate court likely to dismiss the appeal?

choices.A: No, because a TRO is immediately appealable.
choices.B: No, because the 30-day extension makes the TRO equivalent to a preliminary injunction and therefore appealable.
choices.C: Yes, because a TRO is not appealable under the interlocutory appeals statute.
choices.D: Yes, because there is no final judgment from which an appeal may be taken.

questions.explanation:
Final-judgment rule
Rule Appeal only allowed after final judgment
  • If multiple claims/parties, final judgment as to fewer than all claims/parties appropriate if court expressly determines no justifiable reason for delay
Exceptions Interlocutory appeals* concerning:
  • Injunction (grant/denial)
  • Certification by district court
  • Class action certification
  • Appointment of receiver
  • Admiralty case
  • Collateral-order doctrine
  • Bankruptcy cases (certain orders)
  • Mandamus (petition for writ)
  • Patent infringement order (only accounting left)
Mnemonic:  In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely
*Appeal from trial court ruling that occurs before entry of final judgment.

The final-judgment rule bars federal appellate courts from hearing an appeal until the federal district court has entered a final judgment—i.e., a judicial decision that fully resolves the dispute on the merits and leaves nothing for the court to do but enforce the judgment. But the interlocutory appeals statute (28 U.S.C. § 1292) provides exceptions to this rule that allow an immediate appeal in limited circumstances.

One of those circumstances arises when a district court grants or denies a preliminary injunction—i.e., a court order entered before or during trial that commands or prohibits a specified action while the case is before the court. In contrast, a temporary restraining order (TRO)—i.e., a court order that commands or prohibits specified action for 14 days or until a preliminary injunction hearing can take place (whichever occurs first)—is not immediately appealable under this statute (Choice A).

But when a TRO is extended beyond 14 days (as seen here), it becomes equivalent to a preliminary injunction for purposes of an appeal. As a result, the extended TRO is immediately appealable even though there is no final judgment (Choices C & D). Therefore, the appellate court is unlikely to dismiss the lender's appeal of the order extending the TRO.

📌 Educational Objective

The interlocutory appeals statute allows certain orders to be appealed before the entry of a final judgment—e.g., the grant or denial of a preliminary injunction. A temporary restraining order extended beyond 14 days is equivalent to a preliminary injunction and is immediately appealable under this statute.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1292 (exceptions to final judgment rule).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 65 (preliminary injunctions and temporary restraining orders).
  • Sampson v. Murray, 415 U.S. 61, 86–88 (1974) (holding that a temporary restraining order extended beyond its time limit is the equivalent of a preliminary injunction for purposes of an appeal).
  • 11A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2962 (3d ed. 2023) (explaining that a temporary restraining order extended beyond its time limit is the equivalent of a preliminary injunction for purposes of an appeal).

在其房屋即将被止赎拍卖的两天前，一位房主在联邦法院获得了一项临时限制令（TRO），该命令禁止其贷款人在14天内或在初步禁令听证会召开之前（以先到者为准）进行拍卖。当初步禁令听证会未能在最初的14天内安排时，法院将该临时限制令延长了30天。

贷款人对法院延长临时限制令的命令提起了上诉。房主已动议驳回该上诉。

上诉法院是否可能驳回该上诉？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为临时限制令（TRO）是可立即上诉的。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为30天的延期使该临时限制令（TRO）等同于初步禁令，因此可以上诉。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为根据中间上诉法令，临时限制令（TRO）是不可上诉的。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为没有可以据以提起上诉的终局判决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Interlocutory review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：临时限制令（TRO, temporary restraining order）被延长超过14天后，能不能按中间上诉（interlocutory appeal）立刻上诉。

三秒认题路径：

TRO→超14天→像PI→可立刻上诉→不能驳回

核心法律规则

终局判决规则（final-judgment rule）下，通常要等案件结束才能上诉；但28 U.S.C. § 1292给了少数中间上诉（interlocutory appeal）例外。初步禁令（preliminary injunction）的准许或拒绝可以立刻上诉，因为它是在案件进行中直接改变量当事人的行为。

TRO（temporary restraining order）一般不立刻可上诉，但如果它被延长到超过14天，就会在上诉意义上被当成初步禁令（preliminary injunction）。所以这题里，延长30天的命令不是普通TRO，而是可立即上诉的命令。

核心判例： Sampson v. Murray — 说明TRO一旦超过期限被延长，按上诉标准会被当成初步禁令处理。

思维导图

先看：这是终局判决吗？
NO本题还在诉讼中，所以先转向§ 1292的例外。
再看是不是初步禁令（preliminary injunction）？
普通TRO：通常不能马上上诉
但本题被延长30天 → 超过14天 → 上诉上按初步禁令看。
结论：可立刻上诉，不能因“没终局”而驳回。
YES若已终局，当然可上诉；但本题根本不用走这条。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：TRO名字里就写着“临时”，所以一定不能马上上诉。

但考试真正问的是：这个命令在法律效果上是不是已经像初步禁令（preliminary injunction）了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 30天延长 让TRO超过14天，法律上按初步禁令看，所以可以立刻上诉，法院不该驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 TRO 直接当成永远可上诉，忽略了它通常只是例外外的临时命令。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ C: 只盯着“不是终局”就否定上诉，漏掉了 § 1292 的禁令例外。

❌ 事实误判 | 终局状态偷换

✕ D: 把“没有终局判决”当成一票否决，忽略了本题问的是例外中的马上上诉。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问终局，再查法定例外，最后盯住TRO是否已被延长到像初步禁令。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”，先记 Injunction、Certification、Class action 这些法定中间上诉例外；本题就是TRO超14天后按初步禁令处理。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A construction contractor brought a breach-of-contract claim in federal court against a homeowner who had hired the contractor to build an apartment over an existing garage. The action turned on the scope of the work covered by the contract. The contractor and the homeowner were the only witnesses at the bench trial, and they strongly disagreed about the scope of the work. At the end of the trial, the judge stated findings of fact on the record but never issued a written opinion. Neither party objected to the findings. The judge found in favor of the homeowner, and the contractor appealed.
Is the appellate court likely to overturn the findings?

choices.A: No, because the appellate court must give due regard to the trial judge's opportunity to determine witness credibility.
choices.B: No, because the contractor failed to object to the findings when the judge stated them in open court.
choices.C: Yes, because a judge must set forth findings of fact in a written opinion or memorandum of decision.
choices.D: Yes, because there were disputed issues of fact at trial.

questions.explanation:
Jury trial
Jury acts as finder of fact. Judge acts as interpreter of law.
v.
Bench trial
Judge acts as finder of fact and interpreter of law.

In a bench trial, the judge acts as both the finder of fact and interpreter of the law. As a result, Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 52 requires that the judge provide those factual findings and legal conclusions on the record (orally or in writing) after the close of evidence. The appellate court can then review the trial judge's decision under the following standards:

  • de novo (no deference) – where a judge's conclusions of law (eg, elements of a claim) will be reversed if the appellate court reasonably believes that the judge misinterpreted the applicable law
  • clear error (high deference) – where a judge's findings of fact (eg, witness credibility) will be reversed only if they were clearly erroneous such that no reasonable judge would have made them

Under clear-error review, the appellate court must give due regard to the trial judge's opportunity to determine witness credibility because the judge is the one who heard the witnesses' testimony. As a result, the appellate court will likely affirm the trial judge's findings of fact in this suit.

(Choice B) FRCP 52 allows a party to challenge a trial judge's factual findings on appeal even if no objection was made on the record at the bench trial (as seen here). This is an exception to the general rule requiring a party to formally object at trial to preserve an issue for appeal.

(Choice C) In a bench trial, a judge may set forth findings of fact in a written opinion or memorandum of decision but is not required to do so. The findings need only be stated on the record—orally or in writing.

(Choice D) A judge is responsible for resolving disputed issues of fact in a bench trial. Therefore, the presence of such disputes is not a basis to overturn the judge's findings.

📌 Educational Objective

In a bench trial, the judge serves as the finder of fact and the interpreter of law. An appellate court reviews the judge's findings of fact for clear error (high deference) and conclusions of law de novo (no deference).

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 52(a) (findings of fact and conclusions of law).
  • United States v. U.S. Gypsum Co., 333 U.S. 364, 394–95 (1948) (explaining clear-error appellate review).

一名建筑承包商向联邦法院对一名房主提起违约索赔，该房主曾雇佣该承包商在现有车库上加建一套公寓。诉讼的关键在于合同所涵盖的工作范围。在该次法官审判中，承包商和房主是仅有的证人，他们对工作范围的看法严重不一。审判结束时，法官在庭上口头陈述了事实认定，但从未发布书面意见。任何一方均未对该事实认定提出异议。法官最终裁定房主胜诉，承包商随即提起上诉。

上诉法院是否可能推翻该事实认定？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为上诉法院必须适当考虑审判法官判断证人可信度的机会。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为当法官在公开法庭上陈述事实认定时，承包商未能提出异议。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为法官必须在书面意见或判决备忘录中阐明事实认定。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为审判中存在有争议的事实问题。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Scope of review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：bench trial 里，二审对法官的事实认定和证人可信度判断要给多大尊重，尤其是 clear error 还是 de novo。

三秒认题路径：

bench trial → 法官找事实 → 证人冲突 → clear error → 多半不翻

核心法律规则

在 bench trial 里，法官既是 finder of fact 也是 interpreter of law，所以 FRCP 52(a) 要求法官把事实认定和法律结论写进记录里，口头或书面都可以。

二审看事实用 clear error，意思是：只要一审法官亲耳听过证人、还能判断谁更可信，二审就不会轻易改。二审看法律结论用 de novo，意思是：法律对不对，二审自己重新看。

核心判例： United States v. U.S. Gypsum Co. — 它把 clear-error review 的高尊重标准钉死在二审审查事实认定上。

思维导图

先看是不是 bench trial？
是： 法官自己听证人、自己做事实认定 → 二审先问 clear error。
争点是证人谁更可信？
卡死点：法官亲眼听过证言，二审要给“due regard”，通常不翻。
否： 如果是法律结论，才走 de novo，这题不是。
结论： 题干只是在问事实认定能不能被二审推翻 → 选 No。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：双方证词冲突这么大，二审当然可以重来一遍。

但考试真正问的是：这是 bench trial，法官已经当场听过两个人的证词，二审看的是 clear error，不是自己重新选谁更顺眼。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干写明是 bench trial，而且争点只剩证人可信度；这类事实认定在二审按 clear error 看，法官当场听证后通常不会被推翻。

❌ 事实误判 | 漏看规则细节

✕ B: 把 no objection 当成放弃上诉，但 FRCP 52 不要求先反对才能挑战事实认定。

❌ 法律适用 | 书面要求错位

✕ C: 误把口头记录当成必须书面意见，written opinion 不是硬性要求。

❌ 概念混淆 | 把争议当理由

✕ D: 看到 disputed issues 就以为能翻案，但争议本来就是法官要解决的。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓程序姿态：这是 bench trial 的事实认定审查，不是重新审理。

考场速记

记住一句：bench trial 看事实用 clear error，看法律用 de novo；法官亲耳听过证人，二审一般不替他重判可信度。

口诀：“事实看清错，法律看重来；口头写进记录，也能上二审。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A man who owned riverfront property sued an upstream factory in federal court for polluting the river, seeking injunctive relief and $250,000 in damages. The factory moved for summary judgment on the ground of res judicata (claim preclusion), arguing that the man had sued on and lost an identical claim one year before. The court denied the motion.
The factory has asked its attorney's advice as to whether it may appeal the court's denial of summary judgment in order to avoid an expensive trial.
What advice should the attorney give?

choices.A: The factory may appeal if the appellate court finds that the case involves a controlling question of law upon which the courts are divided.
choices.B: The factory may appeal if the trial court certifies that there is no just reason for delay.
choices.C: The factory may not appeal because the denial of summary judgment is a collateral order.
choices.D: The factory may not appeal until after a trial on the merits or other disposition resulting in a final judgment.

questions.explanation:
Final-judgment rule
Rule Appeal only allowed after final judgment
  • If multiple claims/parties, final judgment as to fewer than all claims/parties appropriate if court expressly determines no justifiable reason for delay
Exceptions Interlocutory appeals* concerning:
  • Injunction (grant/denial)
  • Certification by district court
  • Class action certification
  • Appointment of receiver
  • Admiralty case
  • Collateral-order doctrine
  • Bankruptcy cases (certain orders)
  • Mandamus (petition for writ)
  • Patent infringement order (only accounting left)
Mnemonic:  In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely
*Appeal from trial court ruling that occurs before entry of final judgment.

*Appeal from trial court ruling that occurs before entry of final judgment

A party may only appeal, absent limited exceptions, after the district court has entered a final judgment—ie, a decision that fully resolves a dispute on the merits and leaves nothing for the court to do but enforce the judgment. This rule is designed to promote judicial efficiency and avoid unnecessary delays in the litigation process.

Here, the court's denial of the factory's motion for summary judgment based on claim preclusion is not a final judgment. That is because the denial did not fully resolve the dispute on its merits by deciding whether the factory polluted the river and what relief (if any) to award the man. Therefore, the attorney should advise the factory that it may not appeal until after a trial on the merits or other disposition resulting in a final judgment.

(Choice A) A district court can certify (ie, approve) an issue for appeal before a final judgment when (1) there is a substantial difference of opinion on the controlling question of law and (2) an appeal will materially advance the ultimate termination of litigation. Only then will an appellate court decide whether to hear the appeal.

(Choice B) When an action involves multiple claims or parties (not seen here), a district court may enter final judgment as to fewer than all claims or parties if it expressly determines that there is no just reason for delay. A party may then appeal that judgment without waiting for a final judgment to be entered on all claims in the action.

(Choice C) The denial of summary judgment is not a collateral order—ie, a district court order that conclusively resolves an important issue that is (1) separate from the merits of the claim and (2) effectively unreviewable on appeal from a final judgment. That is because an appellate court can easily (and routinely does) review the denial of summary judgment on appeal.

📌 Educational Objective

Absent limited exceptions, an appellate court can only hear appeals from a final judgment—ie, a decision that fully resolves a dispute on the merits.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1291 (final-judgment rule).
  • Lauro Lines s.r.l. v. Chasser, 490 U.S. 495, 497 (1989) (defining final judgment).
  • Ortiz v. Jordan, 562 U.S. 180, 184 (2011) (explaining that almost all orders denying summary judgment are interlocutory orders that do not qualify as final judgments subject to immediate appeal).
questions.zh-question:
一名拥有河滨财产的男子在联邦法院起诉一家上游工厂污染河流，寻求禁令救济和25万美元的损害赔偿。该工厂以既判力（诉讼主张排除）为由，申请即决判决，辩称该男子一年前曾就同一诉讼主张提起诉讼并败诉。法院驳回了该动议。

该工厂向其律师咨询，为了避免昂贵的审判，是否可以对法院驳回即决判决的裁定提起上诉。

律师应提供什么建议？

zh-choices.A: 如果上诉法院认定该案涉及一个各法院意见分歧的决定性法律问题，工厂可以上诉。
zh-choices.B: 如果初审法院证明没有正当理由延迟，工厂可以上诉。
zh-choices.C: 工厂不得上诉，因为驳回即决判决属于附带命令。
zh-choices.D: 工厂在经过案情实质审判或其他导致最终判决的处置之前，不得上诉。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Final judgment rule

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：拒绝简易判决（denial of summary judgment）一般不是终局判决，不能为了省掉审判而立刻上诉。

三秒认题路径：

没终局 → 看例外 → 无法定上诉 → 非附带命令 → 先打完再说

核心法律规则

除非落入少数例外，当事人只能在法院作出终局判决（final judgment）后上诉；考场意思：案件要先把实体争议打完，法院不想让你边打边上诉。

终局判决（final judgment）是那种把争议在实体上一次解决、法院只剩执行的裁定；而拒绝简易判决（denial of summary judgment）只是说“现在还不能直接赢”，不是“你已经赢了”。

这里工厂想直接跳过审判，但法院只是拒绝了它的claim preclusion（res judicata）抗辩，并没有把河流污染、损害赔偿和救济全部解决，所以不能马上上诉。

核心判例： Ortiz v. Jordan — 几乎所有拒绝简易判决的命令都属于中间裁定，通常不能立即上诉。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决（final judgment）吗？
NO 只是拒绝了summary judgment，案件还没打完。
再问 有没有法定中间上诉？
A § 1292(b) certification？题干没有。
B collateral-order doctrine？
卡死点：这里不是 effectively unreviewable，审判后仍能上诉纠正。
YES 才能直接上诉；本题到不了这里。
结论：必须等trial on the merits或其他终局处分后再上诉。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：claim preclusion 看起来很“硬”，输了就白打，所以应该能马上上诉。

但考试真正问的是：这道命令有没有把案件彻底结束；这里没有，它只是让工厂继续打完审判。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

别把“我现在很难受”混成“我现在就能上诉”；能不能上诉看的是终局性，不看诉讼成本高不高。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只是否决了summary judgment，并未终结争议；因此必须等审判或其他终局处分后才可上诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 § 1292(b) 当默认通道，但本题没有 district court certification。

❌ 法律适用 | 最终判决混投

✕ B: 这是多请求或多当事人情形才会用的 no just reason 规则，这里根本不是。

❌ 事实误判 | 附带命令误认

✕ C: 把普通拒绝简易判决硬说成 collateral order，第三要件过不了。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先看是否终局，再逐个排除法定中间上诉和附带命令例外。

questions.question:
A plaintiff brought a diversity action against a defendant in a federal district court for negligence. The defendant demanded a jury trial. At the close of evidence, both parties submitted proposed jury instructions to the court. The court denied these submissions and informed the parties of its proposed instructions. The plaintiff objected, stating that the court's proposed instructions materially misstated the law. The court overruled this objection and delivered its proposed instructions to the jury. The jury returned a verdict in favor of the defendant, and the plaintiff appealed.
On appeal, the plaintiff has argued that the court improperly denied her proposed jury instructions and that the contents of the court's jury instructions materially misstated the law.
What standard(s) of review should the appellate court apply to these arguments?

choices.A: Abuse-of-discretion review as to both arguments.
choices.B: Abuse-of-discretion review as to the denial of the woman's proposed instructions and de novo review as to the contents of the court's jury instructions.
choices.C: De novo review as to both arguments.
choices.D: De novo review as to the denial of the woman's proposed instructions and abuse-of-discretion review as to the contents of the court's jury instructions.

Appellate standards of review
Appeal concerns:

Legal issue

  • Conclusions of law
  • Jury instructions

Fact issue

  • Credibility of witnesses
  • Factual determinations/verdict

Discretionary ruling

  • Injunctions
  • Admissibility of evidence

De novo

  • No deference
  • Reverse if reasonable belief
    judge misinterpreted law

Clear error
(bench trial)

  • High deference
  • Reverse if no reasonable
    judge would have made
    finding

Abuse of discretion

  • High deference
  • Reverse if decision was
    unreasonable/arbitrary

Substantial evidence*

(jury trial)
  • High deference
  • Reverse if no reasonable
    jury would have made
    finding

*Courts may also reverse if there is insufficient or no evidence. Due to this split of authority, this concept is unlikely to be tested.

An appellate court will review a district court's jury instructions under the following standards:

  • Abuse of discretion (high deference) – where the district court's discretionary decisions (eg, the creation of jury instructions) will be reversed if they were unreasonable or arbitrary
  • De novo (no deference) – where a district court's conclusions of law (eg, the contents of jury instructions) will be reversed if the appellate court reasonably believes that the court misinterpreted or misstated the law

The woman's first argument is that the district court improperly denied her proposed jury instructions. Since a district court has broad discretion to decide what language to use in its instructions to the jury, this discretionary ruling should be reviewed for abuse of discretion (Choices C & D).

However, the instructions given to the jury must correctly state the governing law. And since the woman's second argument is that the contents of the court's jury instructions materially misstated the law, this legal issue should be reviewed de novo (Choices A & D)

📌 Educational Objective

On appeal, a district court's discretionary decisions (eg, creation of jury instructions) are reviewed for abuse of discretion while its conclusions of law (eg, contents of jury instructions) are reviewed de novo.

📚 References
  • Crowley v. EpipCent Corp., 883 F.3d 739, 747 (9th Cir. 2018) (explaining that abuse-of-discretion review applies to the creation of jury instructions and de novo review applies to whether the jury instructions correctly state the law).

MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Appeals

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：上诉法院要把 陪审团指示（jury instructions） 拆成两块看——拒绝你自己拟的指示（denial of proposed instructions） 看 裁量滥用（abuse of discretion），指示内容是否把法律讲错（contents misstated the law） 看 de novo。

三秒认题路径：

拒绝拟稿 → 裁量问题 → 指示内容 → 法律对不对 → 两种标准

核心法律规则

先分清 程序性选择（discretionary decision） 和 法律结论（conclusion of law）。法院决定自己用什么语言来写陪审团指示，属于 裁量（discretion），所以看 abuse of discretion，只在决定明显不合理时才改。但指示内容是否正确陈述法律（whether the instruction correctly states the law） 是法律问题，所以看 de novo，上诉法院自己重看，不给原审让路。

核心判例： Crowley v. Epicenter Corp. —— 说明“怎么写指示”看裁量，“有没有把法讲错”看 de novo。

思维导图

题干先把陪审团指示拆成两问：拒绝拟定指示 与 指示内容是否误法。
第一问：法官要不要采用当事人拟的文字？
看 裁量（discretion） → abuse of discretion → 只有不合理/武断才改
本题触发事实：法院 denied these submissions，所以先抓“谁来写指示语言”。
第二问：法官最终写进去的法律对不对？
看 法律陈述（statement of law） → de novo → 法院自己判断有没有误写法律
本题触发事实：原告说 materially misstated the law，所以直接进“法律对不对”的门。
结论：同一组 jury instructions，前半段是裁量，后半段是法律。
答案锁定：B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然都在争 jury instructions，那是不是统一都用一种标准。

但考试真正问的是：“谁决定指示怎么写” 和 “指示有没有把法律讲错” 是两件事；前者看裁量，后者看 de novo。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里 denied these submissions 说的是法官怎么取舍指示语言，属裁量；而 materially misstated the law 说的是法律对不对，直接用 de novo。

❌ 法律适用 | 标准全混用

✕ A: 把“写法”与“对法”都压成 abuse of discretion 了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 法律事实不分

✕ C: 看到 jury instructions 就一刀切成 de novo，忽略了“拒绝拟稿”本身是裁量。

❌ 事实误判 | 角色对调

✕ D: 把“谁来写指示”和“指示写得对不对”对调了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问“法官是在选语言，还是在判断法律对错”，再分别套裁量和 de novo。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“写法看裁量，讲法看 de novo。”

遇到 jury instructions，先拆成 creation of instructions 和 contents of instructions 两层，再下标准。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A bank sued a borrower in federal district court for violating the terms of a mortgage agreement between the two parties. The borrower filed an answer that denied the bank's claim and contained a counterclaim alleging that the bank had engaged in predatory lending in violation of a federal statute. Neither party demanded a jury trial.
At the close of evidence, the judge orally stated his findings of fact and conclusions of law on the record. He found that the overwhelming evidence established that the borrower failed to make her monthly mortgage payments on several occasions during the past year. Based on this fact, the judge concluded that the borrower violated the terms of the mortgage agreement. The judge also concluded that the evidence was insufficient for him to find that the bank engaged in predatory lending. The judge then entered a written final judgment in favor of the bank.
The borrower properly filed an appeal challenging the judge's finding that she had failed to make the mortgage payments.
How will the appellate court likely rule?

choices.A: Affirm the judgment, because the judge is the final arbiter of facts in the absence of a jury.
choices.B: Affirm the judgment, because there was no clearly erroneous finding of fact.
choices.C: Reverse the judgment, because a jury must determine issues of fact.
choices.D: Reverse the judgment, because the findings of fact and conclusions of law were not in writing.

questions.explanation:
Appellate standards of review
Standard Level of review Applicability
De novo
  • No deference to trial judge's legal determination
  • Reverse if reasonably believe trial judge misinterpreted law
 Pure legal issues, eg:
  • conclusions of law
  • content of jury instructions
Clear error
  • Highly deferential to trial judge's factual findings
  • Reverse if no reasonable judge would have made this finding
 Factual issues in bench trials, eg:
  • credibility of witnesses
  • factual determinations
Substantial evidence
  • Highly deferential to jury's factual findings
  • Reverse if no reasonable jury would have made this finding
 Factual issues in jury trials, eg:
  • credibility of witnesses
  • jury's verdict
Abuse of discretion
  • Highly deferential to trial judge's discretionary decisions
  • Reverse only if decision was unreasonable/arbitrary
 Discretionary rulings by judge, eg:
  • grant/denial of new trial
  • admissibility of evidence

The Seventh Amendment right to a jury trial is waived when, as here, no written jury demand is served on the other parties within 14 days after service of the last pleading related to the jury issue. The parties must then proceed with a bench trial, during which the judge serves as the finder of fact and interpreter of the law (Choice C). And after the close of evidence, the judge must provide—orally or in writing—findings of fact and conclusions of law on the record (Choice D).

However, the trial judge is not the final arbiter of the law or facts (Choice A). That is because an appellate court can review the trial judge's decision:

  • for clear error (high deference) – where a judge's findings of fact will be reversed only if they were clearly erroneous such that no reasonable judge would have made them or
  • for de novo (no deference) – where a judge's conclusions of law will be reversed if the appellate court reasonably believes that the judge misinterpreted the applicable law.

And since there was overwhelming evidence that the borrower failed to make her monthly mortgage payments on several occasions, this finding of fact by the district court judge was not clearly erroneous. Therefore, the appellate court will likely affirm the district court's judgment.

📌 Educational Objective

In a bench trial, the judge serves as the finder of fact and interpreter of law. On appeal, the judge's findings of fact are reviewed for clear error (high deference), while its conclusions of law are reviewed de novo (no deference).

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 52(a) (findings of fact and conclusions of law).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Appeals

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：民事案件里，bench trial（法官独任审理）后的事实认定，上诉时是不是按clear error（明显错误）标准看，而不是法官“说了算”。

三秒认题路径：

无陪审团 → 法官找事实 → 上诉审查 → clear error → 看B

核心法律规则

没有陪审团时，法官就是finder of fact（事实裁判者），也负责解释法律；但上诉法院不是“听法官一句算一句”，而是分开审查。findings of fact（事实认定）在上诉中通常按clear error（明显错误）审查，意思是：只有普通理性法官都不会这么认定时，才会改掉。conclusions of law（法律结论）则通常按de novo（重新审查）看。Fed. R. Civ. P. 52(a)要求法官在bench trial后给出事实认定和法律结论。

核心判例： 本题无需背新案名；直接套 Rule 52(a)：事实认定看 clear error，法律结论看 de novo。

思维导图

先看审理结构：没有陪审团，说明这是 bench trial
关卡1：谁在找事实？
法官在找事实，所以不是“陪审团事实认定”那一路
关卡2：上诉挑的是哪一类？
事实认定：有没有漏看证据、明显偏离理性 对应标准：clear error，不是重来一遍自己判
关卡3：题干给了什么？
“overwhelming evidence” 显示拖欠房贷多次
结论：既然证据很强，法官的事实认定不算明显错误
所以：affirm，对应正确选项 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是法官自己认定事实，那上诉法院就不能碰了。
但考试真正问的是：上诉法院能不能按 clear error 改掉这个事实认定，不是问法官是不是“最终裁判人”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「事实在现场看起来有多严重」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的 overwhelming evidence 支持“多次未付款”的事实认定；上诉只看有没有 clear error，这里没有。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“法官审事实”偷换成“法官说了算”。

❌ 法律适用 | 陪审团前提误判

✕ C: 看到 jury 就套上去，但题干明确说双方都没要陪审团。

❌ 事实误判 | 书面要求偷换

✕ D: 把 in writing 当成硬性要求；口头记录也可以。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定是不是 bench trial，再把上诉标准和题干证据强弱对上。

考场速记

记住：bench trial 里，事实认定看 clear error，法律结论看 de novo。

questions.question:
An 18-year-old sued the manufacturer of the e-cigarettes he had vaped for the previous two years in an appropriate federal district court for $1 million. The teenager claimed that the e-cigarettes caused him to develop a serious lung disease. The teenager also alleged that the manufacturer knew the risks posed by e-cigarettes but failed to disclose these risks to its users.
After a trial, the jury returned a verdict in favor of the teenager for $1 million in compensatory damages and $20 million in punitive damages. The judge entered a final judgment in accordance with the jury's verdict the same day.
Three weeks later, the manufacturer filed a motion for remittitur to reduce the amount of punitive damages, arguing that the damages award was excessive and violated the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. The district court denied the motion, and the manufacturer appealed that ruling on due process grounds.
Is the federal appellate court likely to affirm the district court's denial of the motion for remittitur?

choices.A: No, because the judge abused his discretion.
choices.B: No, because the punitive damages awarded were excessive.
choices.C: Yes, because the judge had no authority to alter the jury's award of damages.
choices.D: Yes, because the motion for remittitur was untimely filed.

  • new trial on damages
Additur Plaintiff's request to increase jury award of inadequate damages Never allowed in federal court
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A losing party may file a motion for remittitur within 28 days of the entry of a final judgment to request that the trial judge reduce an allegedly excessive jury award of damages (Choice C). Here, the manufacturer timely filed its motion for remittitur of the jury's punitive damages award three weeks (21 days) after the trial judge entered a final judgment (Choice D). Although this motion was denied, the manufacturer can appeal that ruling.

A ruling on a motion for remittitur is typically discretionary and reviewed by an appellate court for abuse of discretion. But when that ruling is challenged on constitutional grounds—eg, due process—it presents an issue of law that is reviewed de novo (Choice A). A review of the constitutionality of a punitive damages award requires an examination of three factors:

  • The degree of reprehensibility of the defendant's misconduct
  • The size of the award in comparison to the statutory penalties for comparable misconduct
  • The ratio of punitive damages to compensatory damages (this factor receives great weight)

Although the Supreme Court has never identified a precise unconstitutional ratio, it stated in State Farm Mut. Ins. Co. v. Campbell that the ratio generally cannot exceed 9 to 1. Here, the jury awarded the teenager $20 million in punitive damages compared to $1 million in compensatory damages—a 20-to-1 ratio. Therefore, the appellate court will likely conclude that the punitive damages were unconstitutionally excessive and reverse the district court's denial of the motion for remittitur (Choice B).

📌 Educational Objective

Appellate courts apply the de novo standard of review to conclusions of law—eg, that punitive damages were not unconstitutionally excessive. Punitive damages are almost always unconstitutional when the ratio of punitive to compensatory damages is greater than 9 to 1.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(e) (motion to amend judgment).
  • Cooper Indus., Inc. v. Leatherman Tool Grp., Inc., 532 U.S. 424, 435 (2001) (requiring de novo review of punitive damages awards).
  • State Farm Mut. Ins. Co. v. Campbell, 538 U.S. 408, 425 (2003) (holding that punitive damages are likely unconstitutional if they exceed a 9-to-1 ratio).

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：惩罚性赔偿（punitive damages）被主张违反正当程序时，上诉法院要用de novo 还是abuse of discretion 去看，而且这笔奖金额是否真的过高。

三秒认题路径：

终局判决 → 28天内动议 → 宪法挑战 → de novo → 看比例 → 改判

核心法律规则

对remittitur（减额裁定）的决定，平时上诉法院多半按abuse of discretion 看；但如果争点变成due process（正当程序）是否被侵犯，这就成了法律问题，考试上要按de novo 重新看。

判断惩罚性赔偿是否过高，重点不是“法官喜不喜欢”，而是看punitive damages 和compensatory damages 的比例、被告行为恶性、以及可比法定罚则。

这里的关键触发点是：20 million 对 1 million，也就是 20-to-1，明显撞上 State Farm 常说的 9 对 1 经验线，所以上诉法院很可能认定这笔赔偿违宪过高。

核心判例： Cooper Industries v. Leatherman Tool Group 要求对惩罚性赔偿的宪法问题用 de novo；State Farm v. Campbell 提醒你，比例通常别轻易超过 9:1。

思维导图

先看上诉点：这是单纯“法官裁量”吗？
不是：due process 宪法挑战
立刻切换成法律问题 → de novo

1) 被告恶性程度 2) 可比法定罚则 3) 惩罚性 : 补偿性比例
本题比例 20:1 → 超过常见 9:1 线
结论：上诉法院会倾向认定赔偿违宪过高
所以应当推翻地方法院拒绝 remittitur 的决定

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是remittitur，那就是法官自由裁量，二审就只看有没有乱用权力。

但考试真正问的是：这次争议已经升级成constitutional 问题，所以不能只背“裁量”两个字，要直接看赔偿是否因比例过高而违宪。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 20 million punitive damages 对 1 million compensatory damages，比例达到 20:1，明显过高，上诉法院会认定该赔偿违宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 裁量审查误判

✕ A: 把 abuse of discretion 当成唯一标准，忘了这里在审宪法问题。

❌ 法律适用 | 法官权力误判

✕ C: 误以为法官不能改赔偿，忽略了 remittitur 本来就能减额。

❌ 事实误判 | 时限偷换误判

✕ D: 看到 untimely filed 就跳结论，但三周内提起仍在 28 天窗口内。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是“裁量错误”还是“宪法错误”，再用比例线快速筛掉过高赔偿。

考场速记

记住：remittitur 平时看裁量，碰到due process 就切到 de novo；惩罚性赔偿别忘了先看比例，9:1 以上通常很危险。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A computer company fired one of its female employees from her sales position for failing to meet her sales quotas.
The female employee sued the company in federal court, alleging that the company violated a federal law that prohibits sex discrimination in the workplace. Specifically, the female employee claimed that she failed to meet her quotas because the company did not introduce her to potential sales leads or provide her training opportunities in the same way that it did for its male employees. The company conceded that it did not provide the female employee these opportunities but argued that the federal law did not apply to these actions.
After discovery but before trial, the female employee filed a motion for summary judgment. The trial court granted the motion based on its conclusion that the federal law did apply to the company's actions.
The company appealed the trial court's grant of summary judgment.
On appeal, what standard of review will the appellate court apply?

choices.A: Abuse of discretion.
choices.B: Clear and convincing.
choices.C: Clearly erroneous.
choices.D: De novo.

questions.explanation:
Appellate standards of review
Standard Level of review Applicability
De novo • No deference to trial judge's legal determination
• Reverse if reasonably believe trial judge misinterpreted law 		Pure legal issues, eg:
• conclusions of law
• content of jury instructions
Clear error • Highly deferential to trial judge's factual findings
• Reverse if no reasonable judge would have made this finding 		Factual issues in bench trials, eg:
• credibility of witnesses
• factual determinations
Substantial evidence • Highly deferential to jury's factual findings
• Reverse if no reasonable jury would have made this finding 		Factual issues in jury trials, eg:
• credibility of witnesses
• jury's verdict
Abuse of discretion • Highly deferential to trial judge's discretionary decisions
• Reverse only if decision was unreasonable/arbitrary 		Discretionary rulings by judge, eg:
• grant/denial of new trial
• admissibility of evidence

A party can appeal an adverse final judgment issued by the trial court. The standard of review used to review that judgment depends on the issues in dispute. Pure legal issues are reviewed de novo, which allows the appellate court to decide the issue anew without deferring to the lower court's legal interpretation. And the judgment will be reversed if the appellate court reasonably believes that the lower court misinterpreted the law.

A final judgment is the last decision issued by a court that settles the parties' rights and resolves all issues in dispute. This includes summary judgments, where a judgment is entered without a full trial because (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact and (2) the moving party is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. As a result, a grant of summary judgment is a pure legal issue that the appellate court will review de novo.

(Choice A) A trial court's discretionary (not purely legal) rulings are reviewed for abuse of discretion. Under this highly deferential standard, the trial court's decision will only be reversed if it was clearly arbitrary or unreasonable.

(Choice B) "Clear and convincing" is an evidentiary burden of proof—not an appellate standard of review—that is often used in civil suits involving fraud, child custody, and restraining orders. It requires the party with this burden to show that its contention is highly or substantially likely to be true.

(Choice C) The clearly-erroneous standard of review is used to review the trial court's factual (not legal) findings in a bench trial. This standard gives great deference to the trial court, so the court's factual finding will only be reversed if no reasonable judge would have made such a finding.

📌 Educational Objective

The de novo standard of review applies to pure legal issues—eg, grant of summary judgment. Under this standard, no deference is given to the trial court's legal interpretations, and its ruling will be reversed if the appellate court reasonably believes that the trial court misinterpreted the law.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 56 (summary judgment).
  • Borchardt Rifle Corp. v. Cook, 684 F.3d 1037, 1041–42 (10th Cir. 2012) (holding that de novo review applies to appellate review of trial court's summary judgment decision).

zh-choices.A: 自由裁量权滥用。

MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Appeals

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：summary judgment（简易判决）被上诉时，法院要用什么标准审查——这是纯法律问题，所以看 de novo（重新审查）。

三秒认题路径：

简易判决 → 法律结论 → 不让步 → 重新审查 → 选 D

核心法律规则

上诉法院先看这个命令是改事实，还是改法律。de novo（重新审查）的考场意思：上诉法官自己再判断一次，不听一审法官怎么解释法律。

summary judgment（简易判决）之所以走 de novo，是因为它问的是“有没有法律上可直接判”的问题，不是“谁更可信”。

核心判例： Borchardt Rifle Corp. v. Cook——明确说简易判决的上诉审查用 de novo。

思维导图

先问：一审判的是 summary judgment（简易判决） 吗？
是这说明争的是法律结论，不是证人可信度。
接着看No deference（不让步） → 上诉法院自己重做法律判断。
卡死点：不是 clearly erroneous，也不是 abuse of discretion。
结论纯法律问题 → de novo → 选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：一审法官已经做了判断，上诉法院是不是该“尊重一下”他？

但考试真正问的是：这次改的是法律结论，不是事实认定，所以不能套 clear error 或 abuse of discretion。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「一审法官当时怎么看」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 summary judgment 处理的是法律问题；上诉法院不向一审让步，所以用 de novo。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 看到一审就想套 discretion，但这里没有裁量空间。

❌ 法律适用 | 证明标准错位

✕ B: 把 clear and convincing 当审查标准了，它是举证责任，不是上诉标准。

❌ 事实误判 | 事实争点偷换

✕ C: 这题不是在审一审事实认定，clearly erroneous 用错场景了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看一审裁定性质：纯法律问题直接找 de novo，别被“审查很严格”四个字带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：简易判决（summary judgment）上诉 = 纯法律问题 = de novo。看到法律结论、判例解释、规则适用，先想“重新审查”，不是“尊重一审”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A student at a private university sued the university in federal court for negligence after he fell from scaffolding in a university-owned theater building. At trial, after briefing from both parties, the court permitted the jury to hear testimony that there had been several previous accidents in the same building. The jury found for the student, and the university appealed. One of the university's arguments on appeal is that the testimony about the previous accidents should have been excluded as irrelevant and highly prejudicial.
Which standard of review applies to this argument?

choices.A: Abuse of discretion.
choices.B: Clearly erroneous.
choices.C: De novo.
choices.D: Harmless error.

questions.explanation:
Appellate standards of review
Standard Level of review Applicability
De novo • No deference to trial judge's legal determination
• Reverse if reasonably believe trial judge misinterpreted law 		Pure legal issues, eg:
• conclusions of law
• content of jury instructions
Clear error • Highly deferential to trial judge's factual findings
• Reverse if no reasonable judge would have made this finding 		Factual issues in bench trials, eg:
• credibility of witnesses
• factual determinations
Substantial evidence • Highly deferential to jury's factual findings
• Reverse if no reasonable jury would have made this finding 		Factual issues in jury trials, eg:
• credibility of witnesses
• jury's verdict
Abuse of discretion • Highly deferential to trial judge's discretionary decisions
• Reverse only if decision was unreasonable/arbitrary 		Discretionary rulings by judge, eg:
• grant/denial of new trial
• admissibility of evidence

A party can challenge a final judgment on appeal by alleging that the trial court erred. The standard of review used by the appellate court depends on the error alleged. A trial court's discretionary rulings are reviewed for abuse of discretion. Under this highly deferential standard, the trial court's ruling will only be reversed if it was clearly arbitrary or unreasonable. That is because the trial court is best suited to understand the circumstances surrounding the discretionary ruling.

Trial courts regularly make discretionary rulings on the admissibility of evidence—as the trial court did here by allowing the jury to hear testimony regarding the previous accidents. One of the university's arguments is that this testimony should have been excluded as irrelevant and highly prejudicial. Since this argument challenges the trial court's discretionary ruling, abuse-of-discretion review applies.

(Choice B) The clearly-erroneous standard of review is used to review a trial court's factual findings in a bench trial—not discretionary rulings in a jury trial (as seen here). This standard gives great deference to the trial court, so a factual finding will only be reversed if no reasonable judge would have made such a finding.

(Choice C) An appellate court reviews pure legal issues under a de novo standard of review, which allows the appellate court to decide the issue anew without deferring to the lower court's legal interpretation. Evidentiary rulings are not pure issues of law because the trial court must apply the applicable legal rule to the facts.

(Choice D) Harmless error is a conclusion reached by an appellate court when it determines that an erroneous evidentiary ruling did not affect a party's substantial rights. It is not the standard of review that the appellate court applies to determine whether the evidence was erroneously admitted in the first instance.

📌 Educational Objective

The standard of appellate review applies to a trial court's discretionary rulings—eg, whether to admit evidence. Under this highly deferential standard, the appellate court will only reverse a clearly arbitrary or unreasonable ruling.

📚 References
  • Gen. Elec. Co. v. Joiner, 522 U.S. 136, 141 (1997) (stating that "abuse of discretion is the proper standard of review of a district court's evidentiary rulings").

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：证据可采性裁定（evidentiary ruling）在上诉时用什么标准审查。

三秒认题路径：

审上诉 → 证据裁定 → 不是纯法律 → 看裁量 → abuse of discretion

核心法律规则

试题问的是试法院把前次事故证言（testimony about previous accidents）放进来，这属于法官对证据是否采纳的裁量决定（discretionary ruling），考场意思：上诉法院不会自己重做一次判断。

滥用裁量（abuse of discretion）就是“只有明显武断或不合理才改判”；所以只要法官的取舍还说得通，上诉法院通常要尊重。

核心判例： Gen. Elec. Co. v. Joiner — 证据裁定按 abuse of discretion 审查，直接锁定本题答案。

思维导图

上诉人要挑战什么？
先看这是证据是否采纳，不是纯法律解释。
规则法官对相关性（relevance）和偏害性（prejudice）的取舍，属于裁量。
卡死点只有在决定明显武断 / 明显不合理时，才会被推翻。
本题事实法官先听双方简报，再让陪审团听前次事故证言，说明他是在做证据裁量。
结论上诉标准 = abuse of discretion → 选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然争的是“证言能不能进”，那是不是要用 de novo，像在查法律对错一样重新判断。

但考试真正问的是：这不是抽象法条解释，而是法官对证据取舍的裁量问题（discretionary ruling）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 允许前次事故证言进入陪审团，这是证据可采性的裁量裁定，所以上诉只看 abuse of discretion。

❌ 事实误判 | 审判类型看错

✕ B: 把 bench trial 想进来了，这题是陪审团审判。

❌ 法律适用 | 纯法问题偷换

✕ C: 以为这是 pure legal issue，其实法官在做证据取舍。

❌ 概念混淆 | 结案后果当标准

✕ D: 把 harmless error 当成审查标准了，它是先看错没错之后的后果判断。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看“这是法官裁量还是纯法律”，再决定是 abuse of discretion 还是 de novo。

考场速记

记住一句：证据裁定（evidentiary ruling）默认走 abuse of discretion；法官只要不是明显乱来，上诉就很难翻。

口袋口诀：“裁量看 abuse，纯法看 de novo，事实看 clear error。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A motorist sued a police officer in a federal district court for using excessive force during an arrest in violation of a federal statute. The officer moved for summary judgment on the ground that he was immune from suit. The district court entered an order denying the motion and ruling that the officer was not immune from suit as a matter of law. The officer immediately filed a notice of appeal.
Does the appellate court have jurisdiction to hear the appeal?

choices.A: No, because the appeal was not certified by the district court.
choices.B: No, because the district court's decision on immunity is final.
choices.C: Yes, because a contrary decision on appeal could terminate the action.
choices.D: Yes, because an order denying immunity to a government official is an appealable collateral order.

questions.explanation:
Examples of collateral orders
District court orders:
  • denying state 11th Amendment immunity
  • denying government official/employee immunity
  • vacating attachment of vessel
  • refusing to require security bond pursuant to state law
  • remanding action to state court based on abstention

A final judgment generally must be entered before an appellate court can acquire jurisdiction over a case. A final judgment is a decision that fully resolves a dispute on the merits and leaves nothing for the court to do but enforce the judgment. An order denying summary judgment (as seen here) is not final because it merely determines that there is some dispute of material fact—it does not fully resolve the underlying claim. As a result, these orders are typically not appealable.

However, the collateral-order doctrine provides a narrow exception to the final-judgment rule. Under this doctrine, an interlocutory order will be characterized as final and immediately appealable if three elements are met:

  • The order conclusively resolves an important issue (the officer's immunity).
  • That issue is separate from the merits of the underlying claim (whether the officer used excessive force).
  • The order cannot be effectively reviewed on appeal from a final judgment (the officer's claim of immunity will be ineffective once the case has gone to trial).

Therefore, the court's order denying the police officer immunity constitutes a collateral order over which the appellate court has jurisdiction to hear an immediate appeal.

(Choice A) An interlocutory order can be immediately appealed in limited circumstances—including when there is a statutory right to appeal (eg, order granting, modifying, or denying a preliminary injunction), the district court certifies the appeal, or the collateral-order doctrine applies (as seen here).

(Choice B) The district court's decision on immunity is not final because it can be immediately challenged on appeal under the collateral-order doctrine.

(Choice C) The fact that a contrary appellate decision could terminate the action does not provide a basis for an immediate appeal. Instead, the collateral-order doctrine authorizes the appeal at this stage.

📌 Educational Objective

The collateral-order doctrine allows an immediate appeal from an interlocutory order that (1) conclusively resolves an important issue that (2) is separate from the merits of the claim and (3) cannot be effectively reviewed on appeal from a final judgment—eg, an order denying a claim of governmental immunity.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1291 (final-judgment rule).
  • Cohen v. Beneficial Indus. Loan Corp., 337 U.S. 541, 545–46 (1949) (establishing the collateral-order doctrine).
  • Plumhoff v. Rickard, 572 U.S. 765, 771–72 (2014) (explaining that an order denying government immunity is immediately appealable under the collateral-order doctrine).

MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Interlocutory review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：政府官员免疫（government official immunity）被地区法院驳回后，能不能马上上诉。

三秒认题路径：

终局了吗 → 有法定例外吗 → 附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine） → 三要件过没过 → 立刻上诉

核心法律规则

一般要先有终局判决（final judgment），上诉法院才有管辖权；所以普通的中间裁定，考场上默认不能马上上诉。

但附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）是例外：如果裁定已经把一个重要问题一次性定死，而且这个问题和实体争议分开，终局后再审（reviewed after final judgment）就救不回来了，它就能立即上诉。

这题里，免疫不是在问“有没有过失”，而是在问“这个官员现在能不能被拉进审判程序”；一旦先去审判，免疫的程序利益就没了。

核心判例： Plumhoff v. Rickard — 驳回政府官员免疫的裁定通常可按附带命令立即上诉。

思维导图

先看：这是不是 终局判决（final judgment）？
YES → 正常可上诉；但本题不是这个。
NO → 继续找中间上诉例外。
有没有法定中间上诉？
例如 禁令（injunction）、认证上诉、特殊法定授权。
本题 不是这条路，转看 附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）。
三要件能不能过？
1 一次性定死重要问题：免疫已被否定。
2 与实体分开：是否过度用力，和是否有免疫不是一回事。
3 关键卡点：终局后再审也救不回“免疫免于受审”这个利益。
结论
能马上上诉 → 选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然上诉法院改判，案子可能立刻结束，那就应该允许马上上诉。

但考试真正问的是：现在这道裁定有没有被effectively reviewable，而不是以后结果会不会更省事。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以“免疫会被推翻后案件可能终结”不是关键；关键是这类权利本来就主张“先别让我进审判”，拖到终局后再说已经晚了。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干抓到驳回政府官员免疫这个信号；这类裁定满足附带命令原则，所以可以立即上诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把中间上诉硬塞成必须先认证的情形了。

❌ 法律适用 | 终局概念反转

✕ B: 把“免疫被否定”误说成已经终局，太早了。

❌ 事实误判 | 终结结果偷换

✕ C: 盯着terminate the action，忽略了现在能不能上诉。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判终局，再查法定例外，最后只盯附带命令原则的第三要件。

考场速记

记住这句：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，对应的是禁令、认证上诉、集体诉讼等法定中间上诉例外；免疫被驳回也常走附带命令原则。

一看到“官员免疫 / 特权 / 不能等到终局再救”的题，就先想：这是不是 collateral-order，而不是普通中间裁定。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
After a federal trial in which the jury awarded the plaintiff $100,000 in compensatory damages and $7 million in punitive damages, the defendant moved for a new trial on the ground that the verdict was not supported by the evidence and also that the punitive damages award was unconstitutionally excessive. The trial court, after reviewing the evidence, denied the motion on the condition that the plaintiff accept a reduced punitive damages award of $1 million, which the plaintiff did.
The defendant now wants to appeal.
Which of the following principles governs the appellate court's review?

choices.A: The trial court cannot weigh the evidence in ruling on a motion for a new trial.
choices.B: The trial court must give the plaintiff the minimum amount that the jury could have awarded under the evidence.
choices.C: The trial court's decision to reduce the punitive damages award is reviewed de novo.
choices.D: The trial court's reduction of the punitive damages award improperly invaded the province of the jury.

questions.explanation:
Appellate standards of review
Standard Level of review Applicability
De novo • No deference
• Reverse if reasonably believe trial judge misinterpreted law 		Pure legal issues
Clear error • High deference
• Reverse if no reasonable judge would have made finding 		Factual issues in bench trials
Substantial evidence* • High deference
• Reverse if no reasonable jury would have made finding 		Factual issues in jury trials
Abuse of discretion • High deference
• Reverse if decision was unreasonable/arbitrary 		Discretionary rulings by judge

*Courts may also reverse if there is insufficient/no evidence.

A party may move for a new trial on the ground that the finder of fact (typically the jury) awarded an excessive amount of damages. If the trial court rules that the amount was excessive, it must give the opposing party the option to choose between a new trial on damages or a reduced amount of damages set by the court (ie, remittitur). Here, the plaintiff accepted a reduced punitive damages award, which led the court to properly deny the defendant's motion for a new trial.

If an appeal is filed, the appellate court will review the trial court's ruling under the appropriate standard of review. A ruling on a motion for a new trial is typically discretionary and reviewed for abuse of discretion. Under this standard of review, the trial court's discretionary rulings are given high deference and will be reversed only if unreasonable or arbitrary.

However, a ruling challenged on constitutional grounds presents a pure legal issue that is reviewed de novo. Under this standard of review, a trial court's conclusions of law are given no deference and will be reversed if the appellate court reasonably believes that the trial court misinterpreted the law. Since the defendant challenged the punitive damages award as unconstitutionally excessive, the trial court's decision to reduce that award is reviewed de novo.

(Choice A) A trial court may weigh the evidence in ruling on a motion for a new trial.

(Choice B) When reducing the amount of damages that the jury awarded, a trial court has discretion to award any (not just the minimum) amount the jury could have awarded under the evidence.

(Choice C) The trial court's decision to reduce the punitive damages award is reviewed de novo.

(Choice D) A federal trial court has the power to reduce a jury's excessive damages award because the jury has already determined the damages and the court is simply trimming the excess.*

*In contrast, a trial court does not have the power to increase a jury's inadequate damages award (ie, additur) because it would allow the court to award damages that were not found by the jury.

📌 Educational Objective

A ruling on a motion for a new trial is generally discretionary and reviewed on appeal for abuse of discretion. However, when such a ruling is challenged on constitutional grounds, the ruling presents a pure legal issue that is reviewed de novo.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 59 (motion for a new trial).
  • Cooper Indus., Inc. v. Leatherman Tool Grp., Inc., 532 U.S. 424, 435 (2001) (requiring de novo review of punitive damages awards).

现在，被告希望上诉。

下列哪项原则决定了上诉法院的审查？

zh-choices.A: 审判法院在对重审动议作出裁定时，不能衡量证据。
zh-choices.B: 审判法院必须判给原告的金额是陪审团在证据支持下可能裁定的最低金额。
zh-choices.C: 审判法院减少惩罚性损害赔偿金的决定，应进行 de novo 审查。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Appealability and Review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：基于宪法理由（constitutional grounds）去改判惩罚性赔偿时，上诉审查标准（standard of review）是 de novo，不是普通的 abuse of discretion。

三秒认题路径：

新审判动议 → 争赔偿额 → 宪法过高 → 法律问题 → de novo

核心法律规则

一般来说，重新审判动议（motion for a new trial）属于法官裁量，二审通常看 abuse of discretion，也就是只问法官有没有乱来。
但如果争点变成宪法上是否过高（unconstitutionally excessive），那就不是“法官看着顺不顺眼”的问题，而是纯法律判断，所以要用 de novo。
这题里，被告挑战的是 惩罚性赔偿（punitive damages） 的宪法上限，所以二审不会给原审法官裁量让步。

核心判例： Cooper Indus., Inc. v. Leatherman Tool Group, Inc. — 最高法院明确说，惩罚性赔偿是否过高属于纯法律问题，二审按 de novo 审查。

思维导图

先看原审在改什么：新审判动议（motion for a new trial）。
一般规则：法官对是否重审、是否减额，通常有裁量 → 二审常看 abuse of discretion。
本题关口：被告不是在吵“证据够不够”，而是在吵 惩罚性赔偿是否违宪过高。
卡死点：一旦变成宪法问题，就不是裁量问题，而是纯法律问题 → de novo。
结果：原审把 700 万降到 100 万，是在处理法律上限问题；上诉法院自己重新判断，不对原审理由点头哈腰。
答案落点：选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然这是 motion for a new trial，那二审就应该一律按 abuse of discretion。
但考试真正问的是：这次争的是宪法性过高，所以二审要自己重新看法律结论。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「法官当时觉得减得合不合理」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 unconstitutionally excessive 把问题变成纯法律判断，所以减额裁定要按 de novo 审查。

❌ 概念混淆 | 裁量规则误判

✕ A: 把所有新审判动议都当成纯证据裁量了，没看到宪法争点。

❌ 法律适用 | 赔偿下限误判

✕ B: 误以为减额时必须给陪审团可支持的minimum，题目根本没问这个。

❌ 事实误判 | 侵入陪审团误判

✕ D: 只盯着陪审团定过损害额，忽略了被告打的是宪法上限。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓程序姿态，再看争点是不是纯法律；一旦是宪法性赔偿审查，就直接切到 de novo。

考场速记

记住：新审判动议（motion for a new trial）默认看裁量；一旦碰到 惩罚性赔偿（punitive damages） 的宪法过高，二审改用 de novo。
口诀：“动议看裁量，宪法看法律。”

questions.question:
A plaintiff sued a defendant in a federal district court for allegedly violating a recently enacted federal statute. The defendant moved to dismiss the plaintiff's complaint for failure to state a claim. The district court denied the defendant's motion, basing the ruling on a provision of the statute that has been interpreted differently by several district courts. In the written order denying the motion, the district court stated that "there is a substantial difference of opinion on the controlling question of law and an immediate appeal may materially advance the ultimate termination of this litigation."
Forty days after the district court entered this order, the defendant applied to the federal appellate court to hear the appeal of the order.
May the appellate court consider this appeal?

choices.A: No, because only a final judgment can be appealed.
choices.B: No, because the application for appeal was untimely.
choices.C: Yes, because an appellate court must consider an appeal if it is certified by the lower court.
choices.D: Yes, because an immediate appeal is required to avoid protracted and expensive litigation.

questions.explanation:
Final-judgment rule
Did court enter final judgment?
  • Decision fully resolves the merits of a dispute, leaving nothing but enforcement
Yes → Appeal allowed
No ↓
Does exception apply?
  • Injunction (grant/denial)
  • Certification by district court
  • Class action certification
  • Appointment of receiver
  • Admiralty cases
  • Collateral-order doctrine
  • Bankruptcy cases (certain orders)
  • Mandamus (petition for writ)
  • Patent-infringement order (accounting left)
Mnemonic: In Certain Circumstances,
An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely
Yes → Appeal allowed
No ↓
No appeal

Appellate courts may only hear appeals from a final judgment—ie, a decision that fully resolves a dispute on the merits and leaves nothing for the court to do but enforce the judgment—absent limited exceptions.

One exception to this final-judgment rule arises when the district court certifies an interlocutory appeal by stating in a written order that:

  • there is a substantial difference of opinion on the controlling question of law and
  • an appeal may materially advance the ultimate termination of the litigation.

The party seeking an appeal must then apply to the appellate court within 10 days after the district court enters the order, and the appellate court will decide whether to hear the appeal (Choices A & C).* Since the defendant here did not file an application for appeal until 40 days after the district court entered its order certifying the interlocutory appeal, the application was untimely. Therefore, the appellate court cannot hear this appeal.

*An application for such an appeal will stay (ie, halt) the proceedings in the district court if the district or appellate court so orders.

(Choice D) The fact that an immediate appeal may avoid protracted and expensive litigation is not a basis for an interlocutory appeal. In fact, allowing interlocutory appeals may increase the cost of litigation if the litigants pursue repeated appeals instead of filing one appeal after final judgment is entered.

📌 Educational Objective

A district court may certify an order for appeal if it states in writing that (1) there is a substantial difference of opinion on the controlling question of law and (2) an appeal may materially advance the ultimate termination of the litigation. The application to the appellate court must be made within 10 days after the entry of the order.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1291 (final-judgment rule).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1292(b) (district court certification).
  • Liberty Mut. Ins. Co. v. Wetzel, 424 U.S. 737, 745 (1976) (explaining that an application for appeal based on a district court's certification must be made within 10 days after the entry of the order).

MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Interlocutory review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：中间上诉（interlocutory appeal）里，地区法院认证（district court certification）后，申请必须在 10天 内递到上诉法院，晚了就不能审。

三秒认题路径：

非终局 → 有认证 → 看10天 → 40天太晚 → 不能上诉

核心法律规则

上诉法院通常只管 终局判决（final judgment），意思是案件已经把争议解决完，只剩执行。若不是终局，只有少数例外能让你提前上诉。这里用的是 28 U.S.C. § 1292(b) 的认证上诉：地区法院要先在书面命令里写明“控制性法律问题存在重大分歧”，并且“立即上诉能实质推进案件结束”。

但这一步还不够，考场意思：申请人还必须在地区法院命令进入后 10天 内向上诉法院申请。超过这个窗口，就算前面的认证条件都满足，也照样不能立刻审。

核心判例： Liberty Mut. Ins. Co. v. Wetzel — 认证后的上诉申请必须在 10 天内提出，过期就失去中间上诉资格。

思维导图

先看：这是不是 终局判决（final judgment）？
Yes：可以上诉，直接走普通上诉。
No：转去查有没有法定例外。
有无 § 1292(b) 认证？
地区法院书面写明：
1) 控制性法律问题有重大分歧；
2) 立即上诉能加速案件结束。
最后一关：申请是否 10天内 提出？
卡死点：40天 才申请 → 直接超期。
结论
不能审理（No）：认证本来可能开门，但期限没赶上。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：地区法院都说了“重大分歧”而且“能加快结束”，那就应该马上能上诉。

但考试真正问的是：你有没有在法定期限内把申请递到上诉法院。 这题不是在考“理由够不够强”，而是在考“程序窗口有没有踩准”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「立即上诉听起来合不合理」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干已给出认证，但申请人在 40天后 才递交；§ 1292(b) 的申请期限是 10天，所以不能受理。

❌ 概念混淆 | 终局规则误判

✕ A: 只盯着终局原则，忽略了认证例外和期限。

❌ 法律适用 | 强制审查误判

✕ C: 把认证当成法院必须受理，must consider 过头了。

❌ 事实误判 | 目的理由偷换

✕ D: “省钱省时间”不是中间上诉的独立门票。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先认出认证上诉，再立刻查期限，最后看有没有超时。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”，对应 injunction、certification、class action 等例外；但记住，§ 1292(b) 这条路还要再卡一个 10天。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A restaurant owner sued its supplier in a federal district court for breach of contract and trademark infringement. The owner sought $80,000 in damages and a permanent injunction. The supplier filed an answer in which he denied the allegations set forth in the complaint and demanded a jury trial.
The district court denied the supplier's jury-trial demand on the ground that the equitable claim predominated the case. The supplier filed a motion to reconsider, laying out all the precedents clearly requiring a jury in the case. The court entered an order denying the supplier's motion.
What should the supplier do to best protect his right to a jury trial?

choices.A: File a motion for a protective order.
choices.B: File a motion for recusal.
choices.C: File a motion to correct the mistake.
choices.D: File a petition for a writ of mandamus.

questions.explanation:
Final-judgment rule
Did court enter final judgment?
  • Decision fully resolves the merits of a dispute, leaving nothing but enforcement
Does exception apply?
  • Injunction (grant/denial)
  • Certification by district court
  • Class action certification
  • Appointment of receiver
  • Admiralty cases
  • Collateral-order doctrine
  • Bankruptcy cases (certain orders)
  • Mandamus (petition for writ)
  • Patent-infringement order (accounting left)

Mnemonic: In Certain Circumstances,
An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely

Absent limited exceptions, a party cannot seek appellate review of a district court's order until a final judgment has been entered. A petition for a writ of mandamus is one such exception. It requests that an appellate court direct a district court to do or refrain from doing something when exceptional circumstances clearly exist and no other adequate remedy is available. As a result, this writ is appropriate only in extremely limited situations—eg:

  • when a district court clearly exercises unlawful jurisdiction
  • when a district court clearly usurps another branch's power and threatens separation of powers
  • to protect a party's Seventh Amendment right to a jury trial

The supplier should therefore file a petition for a writ of mandamus to protect his jury-trial right.

(Choice A) Protective orders are primarily issued to protect a party from annoyance, embarrassment, or undue expense during discovery. A protective order would not protect the supplier's right to a jury trial.

(Choice B) A motion for recusal requests that the judge presiding over the case excuse him/herself from the case due to bias or prejudice against a party—neither of which is seen here.

(Choice C) A motion to correct a mistake is appropriate when a judgment or order contains a clerical mistake or a mistake arising from an oversight or omission—not an erroneous interpretation of law. Therefore, this is not a basis for the supplier to protect his right to a jury trial.

📌 Educational Objective

An appellate court may grant a petition for a writ of mandamus prior to entry of a final judgment when exceptional circumstances clearly exist—eg, denial of the right to a jury trial—and there is no other adequate remedy.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1651 (writ of mandamus).
  • Dairy Queen, Inc. v. Wood, 369 U.S. 469, 472 (1962) (stating that appellate courts have an obligation to "grant mandamus where necessary to protect the constitutional right to trial by jury").

MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Appealability and Review - Interlocutory review

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：拒绝陪审团审判（denial of jury trial）后，终局判决前能不能用强制令（writ of mandamus）先把权利救回来。

三秒认题路径：

未终局 → 无常规上诉 → 特别救济 → 陪审权受损 → mandamus

核心法律规则

终局判决规则（final-judgment rule）：一般要等案件把实体问题都解决完，才能上诉；中间裁定通常先不能打上诉。

但如果出现极少数例外，尤其是要保护一项现在就会被卡死的权利，法院可以给强制令（mandamus）。考场意思：不是问“这事重不重要”，而是问“现在不管，之后还能不能真正补救”。

本题里，拒绝陪审团审判会直接碰到第七修正案的核心权利，终局后再救往往太晚，所以适合走 mandamus。

核心判例： Dairy Queen, Inc. v. Wood — 需要时，联邦上诉法院应通过 mandamus 保护陪审团审判权。

思维导图

先看：现在能不能直接上诉？
1是终局判决（final judgment）吗？
YES → 直接上诉
NO → 继续看例外
2有没有法定中间上诉？
injunction / certification / class action / receiver / admiralty / bankruptcy / patent
本题没有这些入口
3能不能走附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）？
关键不是“重要”，而是“终局后是否仍可有效救济”
陪审权被拒绝 → 终局后补救太晚 → 用 mandamus
结论
选 D：petition for a writ of mandamus

考点陷阱

你可能会想： 既然法院已经把你的陪审团要求否了，那就赶紧找一个“上诉前救济”凑上去。

但考试真正问的是： 这条路是不是专门针对“现在不救就来不及”的权利；本题就是第七修正案陪审权，所以不是随便找一个动议就能顶上。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 denied the supplier's jury-trial demand，而陪审权是可用 mandamus 及时保护的少数例外，所以应选 D。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 protective order 当成救陪审权的工具了。

❌ 事实误判 | 偏见前提偷换

✕ B: 题干没有法官偏私，recusal 这条线根本没开。

❌ 法律适用 | 纠错对象误套

✕ C: correct a mistake 只改笔误，不改陪审权裁定。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否终局，再找例外；凡是陪审权被错误剥夺，优先想到 mandamus。

考场速记

记住一句：先问终局，再问例外；陪审权被卡死时，mandamus 是最像“立刻补救”的那条路。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，先扫 injunction、certification、class action 等法定例外，再想 collateral-order 和 mandamus。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A business owner sued a federal agency in federal district court, claiming that the agency's recent regulation requiring businesses to report the race and gender of all employees was unconstitutional. The business owner sought a permanent injunction to prevent the agency from enforcing the regulation. At the end of a bench trial, the district court entered a final judgment in favor of the business owner, granting a permanent injunction. Forty-five days later, the federal agency filed a notice of appeal with the clerk of the district court.
How is the federal appellate court likely to proceed?

choices.A: The appellate court will hear the merits of the appeal, because a notice of appeal may be filed within 60 days of the entry of final judgment when a federal agency is a party to the suit.
choices.B: The appellate court will hear the merits of the appeal, because the district court's grant of an injunction is appealable under the interlocutory-appeals statute.
choices.C: The appellate court will refuse to hear the merits of the appeal and will dismiss it, because a notice of appeal of an injunction must be filed within 10 days of the entry of final judgment.
choices.D: The appellate court will refuse to hear the merits of the appeal and will dismiss it, because the federal agency did not file the notice of appeal with the clerk of the appellate court.

questions.explanation:
Deadline to file a notice of appeal
≤ 30 days
Final judgment
entered
→
File notice of appeal
with district court clerk
≤ 60 days
Final judgment

A party may challenge an adverse federal district court ruling, finding, or conclusion by appealing to the federal appellate court encompassing that district. The party must generally file a notice of appeal with the district court clerk within 30 days after the entry of final judgment. However, the time to file a notice of appeal is extended to 60 days if one of the parties is (1) the United States, (2) a federal agency, or (3) a federal officer or employee sued for conduct that relates to government duties.

(Choice A) Here, a federal agency is a party to the suit, so the time to file a notice of appeal is extended to 60 days. This means that the federal agency timely filed its notice of appeal with the clerk of the district court 45 days after final judgment was entered. Therefore, the appellate court will hear the merits of the appeal.

(Choices B & C) An appeal is typically allowed only after a final judgment. However, the interlocutory-appeals statute provides certain exceptions to this final-judgment rule—one of which permits the immediate appeal of a preliminary injunction if the application is made within 10 days of the trial court’s ruling. But this statute is inapplicable here because this permanent injunction constitutes a final judgment—not a temporary ruling.

(Choice D) A notice of appeal must be filed with the clerk of the district court—not the appellate court.

📌 Educational Objective

The time to file a notice of appeal with the district court clerk is extended to 60 days after the entry of final judgment if one of the parties is the United States, a federal agency, or a federal officer or employee sued for conduct related to government duties.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 2107 (timing of appeal).
  • Fed. R. App. P. 4 (notice of appeal).
